On 18th September 2025, this Court (Coram: Kamal Khata, J.) passed the following order :
"1. Astonishingly, in the present Land Acquisition Reference, the Claimant has been awaiting enhancement of compensation since 3rd August 1984 - a period spanning over four decades (41 years).
2. The learned Counsel humbly requests that although the original claim was for Rs.75/- per square meter, the Claimant is now willing to accept Rs. 17/- per square yard, equivalent to Rs.20.33/- per square meter, relying upon the award dated 22nd February 1974 in respect of the acquisition of the adjacent land under the same Notification.
3. By an Order dated 28th February 2020, this Court had already observed that Rs.2/- per square meter was "inconsiderable".

4. Even after a further period of five years, the MHADA has reprehensibly failed to take any decision.
The Claimant is now aged 84 years, has been subjected to shocking and unconscionable delay to say the least.
Justice delayed is justice denied is squarely applicable to this case.
This Court cannot countenance any further inaction.
Each Officer of MHADA responsible for decision-making is answerable for this inordinate delay, particularly when the Claimant has been most reasonable in her demand.
5. Though I was inclined to pass orders against all concerned Officers of MHADA today, at the earnest request of Mr. Lad, one final opportunity of one weeks is granted.

6. List the matter on 25th September 2025.
7.
Mr. Lad is also requested to ensure that, if the decision is taken positively, a pay order in favour of the Claimant is to be brought to Court on the next date so that no further time is lost.

8. It is further clarified that if the decision is not taken and acted upon, this Court will be compelled to initiate such action against all the concerned officers as may be deemed necessary."
2.

Considering the directions issued in the above quoted order, it was expected that the acquiring body i.e. Maharashtra Housing and Area Development Authority (MHADA) would be ready with the pay order in favour of the original claimants.

This appears to be a typical bureaucratic approach bipin prithiani 5-lar-1.13.doc on the part of the office of the MHADA.

4. At this stage, in order to assist the learned counsel appearing for MHADA, the learned counsel appearing for the original claimants handed over a breakup of the enhanced amount that ought to be paid in terms of the observations made in the order dated 18th September 2025.
A copy of the same is tendered for perusal of this Court and the same is taken on record and marked 'x' for identification.
